etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English enmuren and Middle French emmurer, both from Old French enmurer, from Latin immūrō, from in- + mūrus (“wall”). Modern spelling is modelled after the Latin.
senses: (transitive) To cloister, confine, imprison or hole up: to lock someone up or seclude oneself behind walls.
(transitive) To put or bury within a wall.
